target.title: fix(slack): avoid invalid italic boundaries
target.body:
## Summary

- drop only italic style spans whose rendered `_` markers would touch an outer Unicode word character
- preserve the message text and valid Slack italic boundaries
- apply the same normalization to single-message and chunked Slack rendering

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/format.test.ts extensions/slack/src/reply-blocks.test.ts extensions/slack/src/send.blocks.test.ts` (82 tests passed)
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/slack/src/format.ts extensions/slack/src/format.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/slack/src/format.ts extensions/slack/src/format.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Slack displays literal underscores when OpenClaw converts Markdown italics to `_..._` and a marker touches an adjacent CJK or other word character.

Real environment tested: A live OpenClaw 2026.7.1 Slack deployment in a private test channel, using equivalent boundary normalization at the supported outbound hook.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran the source formatter tests above with the observed Japanese sentence, plus the Slack reply-block and send-block suites.

Evidence after fix: The observed source `そう。*「生産性が上がる」という前提が怪しい*んですよね。` normalizes to the same text without visible formatting markers; valid `*重要*。` still normalizes to `_重要_。`.

Observed result after fix: The live agent produced the problematic Markdown form, and Slack read-back contained the intended Japanese sentence with zero literal underscores.

What was not tested: The worktree build itself was not deployed to the live Gateway; live proof used the equivalent boundary rule in a local hook while the source patch was verified with 82 automated tests.
